name: Can I live at home during a bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: Can I stay in my house during a bathroom renovation if I only have one bathroom?
mainEntity.text: Can I stay in my house during a bathroom renovation if I only have one bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can usually remain at home during a bathroom remodel, but the decision depends on how many bathrooms you have and how invasive the work is. If it is your only bathroom, daily life can become difficult during demolition, plumbing rough-in, and final inspections. Many homeowners create a temporary plan using a neighbor, gym, guest bath, or portable shower setup if available. Good contractors will also reduce disruption with dust barriers, floor protection, and scheduled shutoffs for water or power. If you have children, work-from-home needs, or mobility concerns, ask how long the bathroom will be unusable each day and whether any work will happen in consecutive phases. A clear schedule matters more than the total duration because even a short remodel can feel much longer if the room is inaccessible for stretches of time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many homeowners stay in the house during a bathroom remodel, but it is much harder if it is the only bathroom. Temporary shower arrangements, dust control, and clear work hours become important, and the project may be more disruptive if plumbing is shut off for parts of the day.
